assets: the learners' accounts, sessions and progress on tower-data (personal data, DATA-tower-data)
the catalog and its admin routes
the site's secrets, passed to the Lambda as environment variables
boundaries: the browser and the site's Lambda
the site and Google, its only identity provider
CloudFront and the private media bucket

threats.statement: A visitor signs in as someone else, or reaches an admin route without its secret. Residual: the admin API has one shared bearer secret, so whoever holds it is the admin.

A cross-site request, an open redirect after sign-in or an injected script acts with a learner's session. Residual: the content security policy only reports for now, with 'unsafe-inline' scripts, so injected script is held by the framework's escaping, not by an enforced policy; the site sends no HSTS header, so a first visit over plain HTTP can be downgraded.

A catalog change made through the admin routes cannot be traced to the call that made it. Residual: each change writes a catalog_audit row in its own transaction, but the shared admin secret names no person, and the rows live in the database the site itself writes.
A learner's personal data is read by another learner, kept past its retention or processed without a legal basis.
The media bucket is read directly, bypassing the site and the CDN.
A flood of sign-in or admin calls exhausts the Lambda, the database or the spend budget.
A vulnerable third-party package of the site gives an attacker code execution or another user's rights.

The site's Lambda role, or the secrets it holds as environment variables, reach more of the account or the database than the site needs. Residual: the Lambda and its role are not defined in this tree's stacks, so no test here bounds them.

findings.finding: The admin routes are guarded by one shared bearer secret (apps/web/src/admin/auth.ts), not by a person's identity; the model did not say so.
findings.reason: residual added; per-person admin identity is a change of the site.

findings.finding: Besides the report-only policy (stated), the site sends no HSTS header (SECURE-DEFAULTS, CTRL-ssdf-pw.9).
findings.reason: residual added; both gaps are recorded in CTRL-ssdf-pw.9 and are changes of the site.

findings.finding: CHK-web alone does not trace a change; the trace is the catalog_audit row each mutation writes, and it names no person.
findings.reason: the audit's code and table named; residual added.

findings.finding: The media bucket's private access is proved by MediaStackTests, not named.
An asset (the site's secrets in its Lambda's environment) had no threat, and the Lambda's role is outside this tree's stacks.
